messages:
Nora: Hey team — planning my phased return after parental leave and have a couple of benefits/payroll questions. I9m approved to come back 60% FTE for 8 weeks then ramp to full time. Who do I talk to about prorated benefits and payroll deductions?
Priya: Congrats on the return plan, Nora! :tada: Short answer: Priya for benefits/proration, Ben for payroll. A few quick notes: eligibility for benefits continues if you9re on an approved reduced schedule, but some deductions and prorations need HR/payroll coordination.
Nora: OK thanks. Do I need to fill out any forms to switch to 60% FTE temporarily? Also timeline — payroll cutoff is coming up next week.
Ben: Hi Nora — Payroll here. Yes please submit the "Temporary Schedule Change" form (link below) and cc your manager. We need the signed form by the payroll cutoff to change deductions for the coming cycle. If you miss the cutoff, changes apply the next pay period.
Priya: Form link: https://intranet.redwood.com/hr/forms/temporary-schedule-change
Priya: What benefits proration looks like: medical/dental remain active; employer contribution to premiums is prorated based on standard payroll HR rules for partial FTEs. PTO accrual will be prorated during the 60% period. 401(k) contributions are based on actual pay — salary deferral percentage stays the same unless you change it.
Mark: Manager note: I approved the 60% return. Nora, please add the calendar block for core hours and we9ll update on-call rotations. I9ll also add an explicit handoff doc for active tickets so you don9t have to triage everything when you9re at 60%.
Nora: Thanks. Is there any paperwork to keep parental leave continuous so I9m not re-qualifying for benefits? I don9t want a gap.
Priya: No separate paperwork for continuity — the temporary schedule form plus your approved leave record keep things continuous. We9ll attach both to your HR file. If you9re on state leave (e.g., CA/NY) as well as company leave, let us know and we9ll reconcile any state paperwork.
Nora: What about childcare backup subsidy? I9m hoping to use some of it during the 60% weeks for backup care. Any limits?
Priya: Yes the childcare backup stipend can be used during phased return. Reminder: stipend is for emergency/backup only, up to $500 per quarter per employee. Submit receipts to Expenses > New Expense and tag CHILDCARE-BACKUP. Approval is usually 5-10 business days.
Ben: Quick payroll note: if you shift to 60% mid-pay period we pro-rate salary for that partial period, and benefits deductions align to the pay period with the schedule change. If you want net-pay estimates, DM me and I9ll run a calc.
Nora: Great — can you confirm who signs the Temporary Schedule Change? Manager + People Ops?
Priya: Yes: manager signature, employee signature, and People Ops final sign-off. Use the e-sign link on the form or print/sign and upload.
people-ops-bot: Ticket created HR-TEMP-7723 for Nora's phased-return paperwork. People Ops will follow up within 2 business days.
Nora: Awesome, I9ll fill the form and cc Mark. Thanks all :heart:
